title: Reading Entire Payload/File into Memory without Length Limit
pattern: Reading raw streams or files into memory using unbounded read functions (such as `read_to_end`, `read_to_string`, `std::fs::read`) without enclosing the stream in a length-limiting wrapper.
why_bad: Reading files or request streams of arbitrary size into memory exposes the server to resource starvation [59]. If a client uploads a extremely large file (e.g., tens of gigabytes), the read operation will exhaust host memory, degrading system-wide performance and causing OOM crashes [59]. Streams should always be bounded or chunk-processed [209].
detection: Identify instances of `read_to_end` or `read_to_string` on socket streams, file handles, or multi-part upload objects without preceding length limits.
fix: Limit the maximum amount of bytes that can be read by wrapping the reader in a size limiter using the `.take(limit)` method [209].
source: Brendan Gregg, *Systems Performance*, Chapter 7 / passage [59]; Michael T. Nygard, *Release It!*, Chapter 9 (Unbounded Results) / passage [209].
